meta.generated: dashboard-automation compute core (every legacy metric verified vs the historical KQF workbook)
meta.universe_note: Top 100 & the ~90%-cap basket are rebuilt daily from market cap; NSE500 TR is the benchmark.
meta.source: Bloomberg prices/mktcap/volume + broker quarterly fundamentals (Aditya Birla).
caveats: DESCRIPTIVE market-pulse context, not a forward buy/sell signal.

The valuation '90% Mkt Cap' basket covers roughly 86-90% of market cap using only companies that report fundamentals, so it is a slightly different set of stocks from the breadth tab's '90% cap' basket even though the two share a name.
Fundamentals are lagged one quarter; early in a calendar quarter a date may still reference a quarter close to its filing deadline (a mild look-ahead).
The multibagger bands are return thresholds: +200% / +500% / +1000% (about 3x / 6x / 11x the starting price).
'Stocks near their all-time high' measures each stock only from its own listing date, so a newly-listed company is not counted as being near a high on too little history.
Growth-breadth counts profit->loss as a failure (not censored) and blanks buckets with <20 measured names.

plots.title: Aggregate P/E
plots.desc: Cap-weighted P/E of the basket = 1 / aggregate earnings-yield (trailing PAT lagged 1 quarter). Note: '90% Mkt Cap' here is the legacy KQF cumulative-cap basket (fundamentals-restricted; ≈86-90% of total cap — it excludes the single largest name from the 90% threshold). It is NOT the same member set as the breadth tab's '90% cap'. Reconciled to the historical workbook to 1e-15.

plots.title: Valuation breadth: % of stocks expensive
plots.desc: Share of stocks trading at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio above 50x and above 100x, on trailing 12-month profit. Companies that are losing money have no meaningful P/E and are not counted here, so in a weak-earnings period this understates how expensive the market really is; read it alongside the value-breadth and all-time-high panels.

plots.desc: Share of stocks trading below book with ROE above 10% — deep-value-with-quality breadth.

plots.desc: 3-yr CAGR of aggregate capex (annual, broker capex negated).

plots.title: % of firms adding debt faster than equity (3-yr)
plots.desc: Share of companies whose total debt grew by more rupees than their equity did over the last 3 years - a build-up of leverage over time, not a one-year blip. Measured in absolute rupees across the fundamentals universe.

drill.note: firms whose 3-yr debt increase exceeds their 3-yr networth increase. List covers top-1000-by-cap members only; the plotted % counts every covered firm (incl. smaller names, which lever up more often) so it runs ~2pp higher than this list's share.

plots.title: Participation: % of stocks beating NSE500 TR
plots.desc: Share of stocks that beat the NSE500 total-return index over 3 months / 6 months / 1 year. Each stock's return is measured on price alone (dividends not added back) while the benchmark includes dividends, so the bar sits about 1 to 1.5 percent a year too high - read this as a slightly conservative count of how many stocks are keeping up. The 90%-cap series (large, liquid names) is the cleaner read; the all-universe series also includes very short-history names.

plots.title: Liquidity concentration: stocks = 90% of value traded
plots.desc: How concentrated trading is. '% of universe' (default) = the share of all stocks that together make up 90% of a single day's traded value, comparable over time; '# stocks' is the raw count of those names, which can drift simply because the universe grows. The two use different units, so you view one at a time. Measured on a single month-end trading day.

plots.title: Multibaggers: % of 90%-cap stocks up ≥200% / ≥500% / ≥1000% (5-yr low)
plots.desc: Share of large, liquid (90%-cap) stocks whose price is up at least +200% / +500% / +1000% from their lowest point in roughly the last 5 years (about 3x / 6x / 11x off that low). Stocks with less than 5 years of history use their lowest price so far.

plots.title: Stocks near their all-time high
plots.desc: Of the large, liquid stocks (the top 90% of market cap), the share currently trading within 1% of the highest price they have ever reached. Each stock is measured only against its own history since it listed, so a recently-listed company is not counted as being near a high just because it has little history. A high reading means most of the market is at or near record levels; a low reading means very few stocks are.

plots.title: Market-cap share by size bucket (Large / Mid / Small / Micro)
plots.desc: Total market cap split by cap-rank size bucket, each as a share of the day's total cap (Large = Top 100, Mid = 101-250, Small = 251-500, Micro = 501+; the four sum to ~100%). Falling large-cap share with Mid/Small/Micro rising = a broadening market. The cumulative 90%-cap basket is ~flat and drawn in dim grey as a reference. (Single-click any legend entry to hide/show it; double-click to isolate one.)

plots.title: Profitable market-cap share
plots.desc: Share of Top-100 / 90%-cap market cap that is in profit-making companies.

gb.note: Breadth = % of companies in the cap-rank bucket whose trailing PAT (4Q=12m or 12Q=36m) grew faster than the threshold, 1y or 3y-CAGR. A company is measured whenever its PRIOR-period base was positive; a profit->loss deterioration counts as a FAILURE (not excluded). Undefined (excluded) only when the prior base was <=0. Buckets need >=20 measured names (else blank). Fundamentals lagged one quarter.

Breadth = % of companies in the cap-rank bucket whose trailing Sales (4Q=12m or 12Q=36m) grew faster than the threshold, 1y or 3y-CAGR. A company is measured whenever its PRIOR-period base was positive; a profit->loss deterioration counts as a FAILURE (not excluded). Undefined (excluded) only when the prior base was <=0. Buckets need >=20 measured names (else blank). Fundamentals lagged one quarter; financials excluded (interest income != sales).
